content:
The image shows soybean leaves covered with numerous small, reddish-orange to rust-colored pustules/lesions scattered densely across the leaf surface. The leaf background remains mostly green with some yellowing around lesion clusters.

Key visual features:
- Dense, small reddish-brown/orange spots covering entire leaf surface
- Pustule-like appearance, slightly raised
- Uniform distribution across the leaf
- No large necrotic patches or angular lesions

This pattern is characteristic of **Soybean rust** (caused by *Phakopsora pachyrhizi*), which produces numerous small uredinia (pustules) on the undersides and surfaces of leaves, appearing as reddish-brown to tan lesions. The dense, uniform orange-red spotting across the whole leaf is the classic presentation.

This is distinct from Cercospora (which makes larger, more defined angular brown spots) or Septoria brown spot (which tends to be more irregular brown blotches). The density and coloration of these tiny pustules points strongly to rust.
